## What it is

Boîtier de dérivation coffeeflow : quatre Wago 221-423 **debout**, glissés par le haut une fois câblés. Deux aimants 8×3 mm, pas de perçage. Couvercle visé en M3.

## Contexte projet

Quatre potentiels 230 V : phase machine, neutre, phase brew, phase pompe. Détail dans `../../README.md`.

- Imprimante : Bambu Lab A1 Mini, buse 0,4 mm.
- Filament : Bambu Lab PETG HF Black, SKU 33102.
- Vis : **M3 uniquement**. Trou imprimé 2,5 mm, vis autoforeuse, déjà validé.
- Fils : Helukabel Helutherm 145, 0,75 mm², Ø ext. 2,2 mm.
- Montage : on câble le Wago hors boîtier, on l'enfile verticalement, les trois fils se glissent dans la fente en face.
- Châssis ~40–50 °C : deux rails de 2 mm, 1 mm sous le seuil des aimants. Le Wago ne touche pas le fond.
- Fixation machine : friction des aimants, fond local 0,6 mm, dans le canal devant les Wago.

## Design notes

Each 221-423 stands on its 8.3 mm edge (user measurement; datasheet 8.4–8.6 mm). The 18.7 mm lever span is vertical, the 18.6 mm body is pressed against the back wall, wires face the slotted wall. Four **identical** bays of 8.6 mm (0.3 mm extra, close to the 8.3 mm body) with three 0.84 mm murets. Extra length is split across all four bays, never parked at the ends.

Murets are half of the standing Wago **above the 2 mm rails** (2 + 18.7/2 = 11.35 mm from the floor, 9.35 mm beside the connector).

Inner default 37 × 32 mm, walls 1.6 mm, outer 40.2 × 35.2 × 25 mm. Magnet channel is 13.4 mm at the default `largeur` (10 mm is the minimum). A 3 mm raised floor in that channel is the retaining lip (1 mm above the rails) and holds the two wells; floor under each magnet is 0.6 mm. M3 bosses sit on the two outer muret lines, fused into the slotted wall, so they do not widen the end bays. Pillars grow with `hauteur`.

Four open-top slots, 2.5 × 10 mm, one on the centreline of each bay. The lid plate closes them from above.

Bambu Studio warns on nurb 3MF (spec 1.41). Export STL from `print/build/`.

## Don't

- Do not run the M3 holes through the floor. A through-hole left a 0.2 mm cusp at the boss and opens the chassis face.
- Do not polish inner vertical edges. A 1 mm chamfer on 1.6 mm walls left 1.2 mm strips at concave junctions (`concave_cosmetic`). Only the four outer corners are polished.
- Do not enlarge the 2.5 mm M3 holes, and do not switch to M4: M3 already works on this A1 Mini with PETG HF.
- Do not thicken the 0.84 mm murets or the 0.6 mm magnet floor for the min_wall default. Those sizes are the fit.
- Do not let a Wago sit on the floor. The two 2 mm rails are the air gap; a single rail lets the connector pivot.
- Do not put the rails level with the magnet-channel floor. At 3 mm they let the Wago slide out; they sit 1 mm below the 3 mm threshold.
- Do not put the magnet wells under the Wagos. The murets block them; the wells belong in the empty run in front of the connectors.
- Do not close the slots at the top. The three wires have to slide in as the pre-wired Wago drops from +Z.
- Do not run a skirt on the slotted wall of the lid. Slots in the jupe left 0.05–0.12 mm films.
- Do not add extra length at the two ends for the M3 bosses. That made the outer compartments almost twice as wide as the inner ones. Split leftover `longueur` across all four bays, and keep the bosses on the outer muret lines in the magnet channel.
- Do not enlarge the bays much past 8.3 + 0.3 mm: the Wago has to sit calé.
- Do not measure muret height from the floor. The Wago sits on 2 mm rails, so the locating height starts at the rail top (half the standing Wago: 11.35 mm from the floor).
- Do not go back to a three-Wago flat layout. The retired first print is gone; this file is the four standing 221-423.

```toml
[part]
min_wall = 0.6
```
